root_cause: Not MSBuild node count, build-server/VBCSCompiler persistence, TMPDIR/analyzer/terminal-logger/stdin handling, memory, disk, or a hard deadlock. The .NET runtime (dotnet/MSBuild/csc, all managed processes) defaults its GC heap count and thread-pool sizing to the visible processor count (24 on this host); under concurrent load from other lanes sharing the same 24 cores, the resulting large number of futex-synchronized worker/GC threads apparently could not get scheduled fairly enough to make forward progress on this WSL2 host, producing a near-zero-CPU stall that looks identical to a deadlock (S-state threads, one R thread, no OOM/throttle/D-state) but resolves once DOTNET_PROCESSOR_COUNT caps the runtime's own thread/heap fan-out to a small number.
root_cause_evidentiary_basis: Disclosed explicitly per this fix round's review finding: this conclusion is supported by (a) fully retained, independently re-hashed evidence that the fix works -- attempts 6 and 7 both succeeded with DOTNET_PROCESSOR_COUNT=2 set, on an isolated probe and the full solution respectively, both wrapper logs retained and re-verified this round, and attempt 7's Launcher.dll re-hashed live from disk -- and (b) operator-reported, NOT independently re-verifiable, prose that attempts 1-3 and 5 hung with near-identical qualitative signatures without that variable set (attempt 4 differs slightly: a hard 600s timeout(1) rather than an operator kill, also not independently re-verifiable). The specific quantitative claims for the hangs (thread counts, cgroup CPU-usage figures, memory figures) are NOT backed by any retained artifact for any of attempts 1-5; see build_attempts[].artifact_status for the per-attempt breakdown and build_attempts_evidence_summary for why this round did not attempt a fresh reproduction to backfill them. The causal claim itself (unset/default DOTNET_PROCESSOR_COUNT reproducibly hangs Common's compile on this host under contention; DOTNET_PROCESSOR_COUNT=2 reproducibly does not) is therefore evidenced by a real before/after contrast, but the specific numbers describing the 'before' side rest on operator observation from earlier rounds' sessions, not on anything this receipt or the private run dir can independently reproduce.
limitations: PRIMARY: attempts 1-4 (and attempt 5's fine-grained cgroup/proc figures) have no retained wrapper log, output file, or sha256 anywhere in the repository or the private run dir; they are operator-observed prose from earlier rounds' sessions and are not independently re-verifiable from this receipt. This was raised as a major finding twice (once as a previously 'unresolved' item, once as a new major finding) and is not fully closed by this fix round: no new reproduction was attempted (see build_attempts_evidence_summary for why), so this remains a real, disclosed gap rather than a resolved one. What this round did do: hashed every artifact that IS retained (attempts 5, 6, 7), independently re-verified attempt 7's Launcher.dll live from disk, and made the per-attempt evidentiary status explicit instead of implicit.

Root-cause diagnosis rests on a single successful reproduction path (DOTNET_PROCESSOR_COUNT=2 on both an isolated single-project probe and the full solution) plus (operator-reported, not independently retained) hangs without it; a controlled sweep (e.g. DOTNET_PROCESSOR_COUNT=1,2,4,8 with and without host contention) was not run, so the exact contention threshold is not established -- only that 2 works and unset does not, on this shared host, at this observed load.

The existing tools/lean-985ef30 and tools/lean-985ef30-remediation roots were not rebuilt or compared against for this diagnosis; the 7730-warning match against resolution.md's recorded count is a strong but indirect cross-check, not a rebuild of those roots.

This is a local integration build on one pinned commit plus the recorded remediation patch, not a general fix for QuantConnect/Lean's upstream build, and not evidence that every WSL2/many-core host exhibits this stall.
